clue.text: Hard contest overwhelms old linesman

indicators.note: to overwhelm here is to swamp or engulf, so the hard contest wraps round the old

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
a race is a contest of speed

explanation.surface: A tough competition gets the better of an elderly assistant referee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Linesman' suggests a football official, but here it is a man of lines of verse: the Roman poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A poet writes lines of verse, and this Roman lyric poet is a celebrated one.

clue.text: "But why thy — matcheth not thy show, / The folly's this, that thou doest common grow" (Shakespeare)

definitions.text: "But why thy — matcheth not thy show, / The folly's this, that thou doest common grow" (Shakespeare)

parts.words: "But why thy — matcheth not thy show, / The folly's this, that thou doest common grow" (Shakespeare)
parts.note: the closing couplet of Shakespeare's Sonnet 69, with the missing word being the scent or smell of the beloved, set against outward show

explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: supply the missing word from Sonnet 69, where the youth's inner reputation (his smell, metaphorically) fails to match his fair appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: The sonnet contrasts outward show with the scent or reek of the youth's behaviour, the word that fills the gap.

clue.text: A small price to take home lawyer turned historical novelist

indicators.note: to take something in is to admit it, so these pieces receive the word for home into their midst

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
worth means value or price
in means at home

explanation.surface: A modest fee persuades a solicitor to turn to writing period fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: William Harrison Ainsworth trained as a solicitor before writing historical romances such as Old St Paul's, so the whole phrase is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrison Ainsworth qualified in law, then became a prolific Victorian author of historical romances.

clue.text: "He, who to seem more deep than you or I, / - old bards, or Merlin's Prophecy" (Pope)

definitions.text: "He, who to seem more deep than you or I, / - old bards, or Merlin's Prophecy" (Pope)

parts.words: "He, who to seem more deep than you or I, / - old bards, or Merlin's Prophecy" (Pope)
parts.note: lines from Pope's Imitations of Horace, where the missing verb is the pretentious man's lavish praising of ancient poets

explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue from Pope's imitation of Horace's epistle to Augustus: the would-be deep thinker praises old bards to look learned.
explanation.definitionFit: The man showing off his depth praises highly, or lauds, the old bards and Merlin's prophecy.

clue.text: Artful writer is excellent describing line by Morrissey?

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round, so the excellent word goes round the line

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as the letters A and I
Morrissey sang with The Smiths, so he was one of them, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A writer is praised for a lyric written by the singer Morrissey.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-rate) is taken as AI. Ali Smith wrote Artful, a book of lectures on art and fiction, so 'Artful' is the title, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish author Ali Smith published Artful, so she is that book's writer.

clue.text: Novel description of Chardonnay that has age?

parts.note: Chardonnay is typically a dry white wine
a season is a period or time, an age

explanation.surface: A wine writer describes a mature Chardonnay.
explanation.walkthrough: André Brink's novel about apartheid South Africa; the clue pretends to be a wine note.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dry White Season is a 1979 novel by the South African writer André Brink.

clue.text: Book about a man thinking of leaving his wife one city man trashed

definitions.text: Book about a man thinking of leaving his wife

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: trashed means wrecked, so the letters are smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A novel tells of a husband planning to walk out, while a City worker is ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the plot: Hanif Kureishi's 1998 novella follows a man on his last night before leaving his partner; 'trashed' is the anagram signal, not a comment on the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanif Kureishi's Intimacy follows a man on the night before he deserts his family.

clue.text: Marvel artist's not over nuking originally cave-dwelling Avenger

annotationWithheld.why: Marvel artist's not over nuking originally cave-dwelling Avenger (5): MANON (Manon des Sources) fits 'cave-dwelling Avenger', but no parse of 'Marvel artist's not over nuking originally' giving MANON was found and no blog or database explains it
annotationWithheld.clue: Marvel artist's not over nuking originally cave-dwelling Avenger

clue.text: Row around tip of bleak Scottish island to see Tacy's pal

indicators.note: the row goes around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Mull is an island of the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: A tier of seats surrounds the edge of a bleak Scottish island, for the sake of a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Tib Muller is the third friend in Maud Hart Lovelace's Betsy-Tacy children's books.
explanation.definitionFit: In Lovelace's Betsy-Tacy series, Tib is the friend of Betsy and Tacy.

clue.text: Academic article about prostitute by Time writer of demi-monde themes

parts.note: a don is a university academic

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the article runs backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a tart is slang for a prostitute

explanation.surface: A scholarly piece about a sex worker appears beside a Time magazine author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses AN to NA. Donna Tartt's novels, The Secret History and The Goldfinch, deal with the shady fringes of society.
explanation.definitionFit: Donna Tartt is an American novelist whose books explore murky, half-respectable worlds.

clue.text: Small book popular all over is Writer's Tips

indicators.note: all over here means turned over completely, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A slim volume of advice for authors is a bestseller everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over' turns S, B and IN round as one run, SBIN, to give the points of pens; 'Writer's' means the pen, not an author.
explanation.definitionFit: The points of fountain pens, which do the writing, are their nibs.

clue.text: Guardian is contemptible going after old Scottish PM

indicators.note: going after means following, so this piece comes behind the prime minister

parts.note: Gordon Brown, the Scottish politician, was UK prime minister 2007-10
low means mean or despicable

explanation.surface: A protector is despised, chasing a former British leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Brownlow is Oliver Twist's benevolent protector in Dickens; 'Guardian' is not the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: In Dickens's Oliver Twist, Mr Brownlow takes the orphan in and becomes his protector.

clue.text: Chap volunteers to guard university in Virgil's hometown

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: to guard is to surround protectively, so the volunteers enclose the university

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A man and some reservists protect a college in the poet's birthplace.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin poet Virgil was born near Mantua in northern Italy.

clue.text: King Edward?

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's tragic monarch who divides his kingdom
Edward ___, the Victorian nonsense poet, a first name needing its surname, hence the question mark

explanation.walkthrough: 'King Edward' looks like a monarch or a potato variety; it splits into two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Both Shakespeare's tragic king and the nonsense-verse writer Edward share this name.

clue.text: I laze around with Mole, who worked up the soil

indicators.note: around means moved about, so these words' letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Kenneth Grahame's Mole and I idle about together, digging the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: Mole looks like Kenneth Grahame's burrower, the one 'working the soil', but he is fodder; the French novelist wrote La Terre (The Earth) and Germinal, about miners.
explanation.definitionFit: The French naturalist novelist wrote La Terre about peasant farming and Germinal about coal mining.

clue.text: I wrote of love and marriage within church without locks

definitions.text: I wrote of love and marriage

parts.note: in means within
having no locks of hair is to be bald

explanation.surface: A writer speaks of romance and wedlock, inside a church whose doors are unlocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without locks' suggests an unlocked door, but it means hairless. Elizabeth Inchbald wrote A Simple Story, about love and marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Inchbald's novel A Simple Story treats courtship and wedlock, so she speaks for herself here.

clue.text: British career fit for the stage manager of Westfield's Men

definitions.text: the stage manager of Westfield's Men

parts.note: to career is to rush along, to race
fit means healthy, well

explanation.surface: A British career suited to the theatre manager of a company.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicholas Bracewell is the book holder of Lord Westfield's Men in Edward Marston's Elizabethan theatre mysteries; 'career' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In Edward Marston's mysteries, Nicholas Bracewell runs backstage for the acting troupe Westfield's Men.

clue.text: Spirit and second lump of ice for a member of the beats

parts.note: gin is a spirit
a berg is an iceberg

explanation.surface: A gin and a second ice cube for a jazz-age poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the beats' is the Beat Generation, not rhythm. Allen Ginsberg wrote Howl.
explanation.definitionFit: Allen Ginsberg was a leading poet of the American Beat Generation.

clue.text: Stoned English teacher read back story of social degradation

parts.note: stoned means intoxicated, high

indicators.note: read back means read in reverse, so the pair of pieces runs backwards

parts.note: sir is a schoolchild's name for a male teacher

explanation.surface: An intoxicated English master reads out a novel about a society's collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read back' turns E and SIR to make RISE. J G Ballard's novel shows the residents of a tower block descending into savagery.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballard's 1975 novel depicts the tenants of a tower block descending into tribal violence.

clue.text: Pretensions people like Paul Dombey Jr. picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the clue gives a word said out loud

parts.note: Paul Dombey junior is the son and heir of the firm in Dickens's Dombey and Son

explanation.surface: Affectations that children like Dickens's young Paul Dombey acquired.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for inheritors sounds like the answer when the H is dropped, as in non-rhotic British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on affected manners is to give oneself pretensions.

clue.text: To her friends, Renard is pleasant without touches of old languor

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the pleasant word lies outside the other letters

parts.note: nice means pleasant

indicators.note: the touches of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Friends say Renard is agreeable once she sheds her old lethargy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but it means outside, so NICE wraps O and L. The definition is a woman surnamed Renard, known by her first name to her friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Friends use a woman's first name, so this given name is how Renard is addressed informally.

clue.text: Female with awful urges in tale of Fadden's haunting

indicators.note: awful means terrible, so the letters are rearranged badly

explanation.surface: A woman with terrible cravings appears in a ghost story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges URGES after F. Brian Moore's novel Fergus has a writer, Fergus Fadden, haunted by figures from his past.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Moore's 1970 novel follows the novelist Fergus Fadden, haunted by apparitions of his family.

clue.text: Two different soldiers producing oil-coloured work?

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier; a soldier ant is a kind of ant
a GI is an American soldier; a soldier ant is a kind of ant

explanation.surface: Two kinds of soldier produce a painting in oils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oil-coloured' suggests an oil painting, but Edna Ferber's novel is coloured by Texas oil money.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna Ferber's novel Giant is steeped in the Texas oil boom, so it is a book tinged with oil.

clue.text: Nice men kicked around European title for Thomas Wolsey

indicators.note: kicked around means knocked about, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Pleasant men knock a European about over the cardinal's honorific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kicked around' is the anagram signal, and the shuffle leaves one E still to add. Cardinals such as Wolsey are addressed as 'Your Eminence'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinals are formally styled by this honorific, and Wolsey was a cardinal under Henry VIII.

clue.text: Company secures revolutionary epic of 7th-century religion

indicators.note: secures means holds fast, so the company encloses the revolutionary

parts.note: red is a communist, a revolutionary

explanation.surface: A firm holds a radical novel about early Christianity.
explanation.walkthrough: Melvyn Bragg's novel Credo is set in seventh-century Britain at the coming of Christianity.
explanation.definitionFit: Melvyn Bragg's sprawling novel Credo tells of faith in Dark Age Britain.

clue.text: Old lady going around performing as an Angie Mitchell ook-a-like

indicators.note: going around means encircling, so the old lady surrounds the performing word

parts.note: ma is a mother, an old lady in slang
on means performing, as on stage

explanation.surface: A mother takes to the stage as a double for a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ook-a-like' is the clue's printed slip for 'look-alike'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman bearing this first name is offered as a double for a named person, a given name used as a lookalike.

clue.text: Hack fetes Dean, having screened opening of Oscar-nominated book adaptation

indicators.note: to screen is to hide behind cover, so the shuffled letters enclose the opening
to hack is to chop up, so the letters are cut and rearranged
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A journalist praises James Dean, who starred in a screen version of a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' looks like a journalist but is the anagram signal; 'having screened' puts the O inside. James Dean starred in the 1955 film of Steinbeck's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1955 Elia Kazan film was made from John Steinbeck's novel.

clue.text: Singer a nasty type knocked over close to Jonathan Ross's producer

parts.note: a rat is an informer, one who sings to the police

indicators.note: knocked over means upended, so this pair of pieces runs backwards

parts.note: a git is a nasty person

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An informer turns on a nasty type near Jonathan Ross's TV producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns A GIT into TIGA. Ross is Terence Rattigan's play about T. E. Lawrence, not the talk-show host Jonathan Ross.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence Rattigan wrote the 1960 play Ross, about Lawrence of Arabia.

clue.text: Scottish poet is flipping grafter mostly, head of Ladybird admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the head of Ladybird goes inside
flipping means turning over, so the word reads backwards
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a toiler is a hard worker, a grafter

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Scottish poet is turning into a hard worker, led by a children's book publisher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts TOILER to TOILE, 'flipping' turns it to ELIOT, and 'admitted' takes in L. Jean Elliot wrote the Scots lament The Flowers of the Forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Elliot was an 18th-century Scottish writer of verse, author of a famous lament.
